key_concepts: Matter is made of atoms composed of protons, neutrons, and electrons
Protons are positively charged, electrons are negatively charged, and neutrons are neutral
Objects are neutral when they have equal numbers of protons and electrons
An object with more electrons is negatively charged; more protons is positively charged
Electrons can move or be rubbed off between materials
Rubbing a balloon transfers electrons, making it negatively charged
A charged object creates an electric field around it
Electric field strength decreases with distance from the charged source
A negatively charged balloon repels negative charges in a wall, leaving a positive area
Opposite charges attract, causing the balloon to stick to the wall
Static electricity is a buildup of charge or a spark from charge buildup
Some materials lose electrons more easily and charge balloons better, such as wool, cotton
